findings.reason: the plan must state that the single oras list is version-sorted (or that these two queries sort it) before it can claim the copied machine is safe over an unsorted registry tag list.
findings.text: §18 says "one function lists the package's tags with `oras repo tags` ... and every tag query in the copied machine reads that one list: the latest tag (`_get_latest_tag`), the latest stable tag (`_get_latest_stable_tag`)", but those two functions in the copied machine depend on the version ordering that `git tag --sort=-v:refname` supplied (`_get_latest_tag` release.py:29-42, `_get_latest_stable_tag` :45-58 take the first match in sorted order); `oras repo tags` returns tags in registry order, so "the latest tag" becomes undefined and `compute_next_version` (release.py:153) can pick the wrong base and compute a next version that re-collides with an existing tag or steps backwards

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the author mirror its empty-list and annotation-key conventions (and say whether ambix can depend on it) rather than fork a second, drifting oras layer.
findings.text: the map release CLI re-implements the GHCR operations that already live in `ghcr.py`: `list_registry_tags` (:335, the exact `oras repo tags` call §18 specifies, including its `not found` → `[]` handling that the "with no semver tag ... stable at `v0.0.0`" start state needs), `fetch_tag_messages` (:355, the `oras manifest fetch` annotation read that §18's `status` and its push annotation require), `login_to_ghcr` (:230) and `require_oras` (:205); §18 names `release.py` as the source it copies but never names this owner, so the new module re-derives the registry conventions

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one new module `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py` hides the registry protocol, the CLI state machine and the tree digest behind three commands (`release`, `pull`, `status`), and the machine-to-package table is placed with its sibling map constants in `imas_ambix/data/paths.py`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the oras tag listing, manifest-annotation read, ghcr login and oras presence check §18 adds are already owned by `imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py` (`list_registry_tags` :335, `fetch_tag_messages` :355, `login_to_ghcr` :230, `require_oras` :205) and §18 names no owner to extend or mirror.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §18's "Accounting for the new surface" paragraph names the installer pull path it retires by merging into `maps pull`, states that `release`/`status` are capabilities with no command to retire, and gives the reason the one added refusal cannot be retired.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §18 cites the state machine in `imas_codex/cli/release.py` but not `imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py`, which already owns the `oras repo tags` listing, the manifest-annotation read and the ghcr login the new map CLI is about to re-add; and the copied tag queries depend on a version ordering the git query supplied and the oras list does not.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `maps pull`/`maps release` justify themselves: §18 merges `packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh`'s private `oras pull` into `maps pull --dest` so "the registry, the auth form and the artifact type have one owner", and it is that write path the section names.
